data.name: Prostate cancer
data.description: Cancer in which oncogenic mTOR signaling reprograms the cell's translation to drive proliferation, invasion and metastasis.
data.description_beginner: A cancer in which mTOR signaling gets hijacked to rev up a tumor's protein-building machinery, helping it grow, invade nearby tissue, and spread.

studies.title: The translational landscape of mTOR signalling steers cancer initiation and metastasis
studies.authors: Hsieh AC; Liu Yi; Edlind MP; Ingolia NT; Janes MR; Sher A; et al.; Ruggero D

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.finding: Showed WHY mTOR-driven translation matters for cancer: in prostate cancer, oncogenic mTOR selectively translates a specific set of pro-invasion mRNAs that drive metastasis. An ATP-competitive mTOR inhibitor (INK128) reversed that signature - an early preclinical rationale from mouse models and cell lines, not a clinical result.

studies.title: mTOR complex 2 is required for the development of prostate cancer induced by Pten loss in mice
studies.authors: Guertin DA; Sabatini DM et al.

evidence.label: Animal model
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.finding: mTORC2 is required for prostate cancer driven by Pten loss in mice.

studies.title: mTOR inhibition reverses Akt-dependent prostate intraepithelial neoplasia through regulation of apoptotic and HIF-1-dependent pathways
studies.authors: Majumder PK; Sellers WR et al.

evidence.label: Animal model
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.finding: mTOR inhibition (rapamycin/RAD001) reverses Akt-driven prostate intraepithelial neoplasia in mice.

relations.mechanism: Blocking mTOR reversed Akt-driven pre-cancerous prostate lesions in mice, showing the growth was mTORC1-dependent and reversible.
relations.mechanism_beginner: Blocking mTOR reversed early, pre-cancerous prostate changes in mice caused by an overactive growth signal.
relations.boundary: Scope: the lesion was prostatic intraepithelial neoplasia, a pre-cancerous stage, driven by transgenic human AKT1 in mice, and the drug (RAD001) inhibits mTORC1 allosterically. Mouse only in this corpus. Not a demonstration in established prostate cancer.
relations.note: The arrow means mTORC1 inhibition reversed a pre-cancerous prostate lesion in a mouse model. It is not a claim that mTORC1 drives established prostate cancer.

relations.mechanism: Prostate cancer driven by Pten loss needs mTORC2 to develop; normal prostate does not. A real therapeutic window, at least in mice.
relations.mechanism_beginner: Prostate tumours caused by losing a specific tumour-suppressor gene (Pten) need mTORC2 to develop – normal prostate tissue doesn't, at least in mice.
relations.boundary: Single-study edge in this corpus (GUE2009). Shown in Pten-null mouse prostate only: mTORC2 (Rictor) is required for tumours to develop in that genetic background, while normal prostate epithelium is not dependent on it. Mouse only - not tested in another species in this corpus, and not shown in human prostate cancer.
relations.note: The arrow means mTORC2 is required for Pten-loss-driven prostate cancer to develop in mice. It does not claim that mTORC2 causes prostate cancer, and it says nothing about human disease.
